Definition: from derivative of φθίνω (to wane; akin to the base of G5351) and G3703 (meaning late autumn); autumnal (as stripped of leaves):--whose fruit withereth.
BiblicalUsage: Phthinoporinos means autumnal, stripped of leaves, past fruit. Jude uses it once, in Jude 1:12, for false teachers at the love feasts: trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a tree with no fruit in its season is the plainest picture of a teacher with nothing to give.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
